item.title: Profinite groups with finite conjugacy classes of commutators
item.description: arXiv:2611.13133v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It was shown in a recent work by Senise and Shumyatsky that if $G$ is a finite group such that $|x^G|\leq m$ whenever $x$ is a commutator of prime power order, then $G''$ has $m$-bounded order. In this paper, we examine the following question: given a profinite group $G$ such that $|x^G|$ is finite whenever $x$ is a commutator of prime power order, does it follow that $G''$ is finite? We show that, in general, the answer to this is negative. The main result obtained in this paper is the following theorem: Let $G$ be a profinite group in which $|x^G|$ is finite whenever $x$ is a commutator of prime power order. Assume that $\pi(G)$ is finite. Then: (1) The second commutator subgroup $G''$ is finite; (2) $G$ has an open normal subgroup of nilpotency class at most $3$.
item.dc:creator: Eloisa Detomi, D\'ebora Senise, Pavel Shumyatsky

item.title: Smooth actions of Baumslag-Solitar groups on the interval
item.description: arXiv:2611.13171v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study representations of the Baumslag-Solitar group $BS(m,n)=\langle a,b\mid ab^ma^{-1}=b^n\rangle$ inside the group of orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of the interval $[0,1]$. We prove that for integers $n,m\in \mathbb Z\setminus\{-1,0,1\}$, the group $BS(m,n)$ embeds into $\mathrm{Diff}_+^1([0,1])$ if and only if $|n|=|m|$. Furthermore, we show that for any $\alpha\in (0,1)$, the group $BS(m,n)$ embeds inside $\mathrm{Diff}_+^{1+\alpha}([0,1])$ if and only if $1=|m|=|n|$ or when $1=m\leq n$.
item.dc:creator: Franco G\'omez, Crist\'obal Rivas

item.title: On Distinct Powers in Finite Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.13582v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sun conjectured that if a group $G$ has no elements of orders $2,3,...,n+1$, then every $n$-element subset $A$ can be ordered as $a_1,...,a_n$ so that $a_1,a_2^2,...,a_n^n$ are pairwise distinct. We prove the conjecture for finite groups when $n=4,5,6$. The proofs combine collision-counting arguments with reductions to finite-field assignment problems; the remaining finite cases for $n=6$ are verified exhaustively. We also prove the conjecture for every $n$ when no four elements of $A$ generate the same cyclic subgroup.
item.dc:creator: Dingying Ma

item.title: A congruence-group counterexample to Kourovka Problem 21.7
item.description: arXiv:2611.13792v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every prime $p>24$, let $H$ be the kernel of $\SL_2(\Z/p^9\Z)\to\SL_2(\F_p)$. We prove that $H$ is not IYB, whereas $H\times C_{p^8}$ is IYB. The proof excludes a pre-Lie multiplication on the rank-three Lie ring with bracket $p[x,y]$ over $\Z/p^8\Z$ using three trace identities. It follows that the supersoluble group $H\times(C_{p^8}\rtimes C_2)$, with the involution acting by inversion, has IYB Sylow subgroups and is not IYB. Its nilpotent residual is cyclic and its Sylow $p$-subgroup has nilpotency class eight. For $p=31$, an action of order three gives a supersoluble counterexample of odd order $3\cdot31^{32}$. The same construction gives an IYB $p$-group with a specified central cyclic direct factor such that the quotient of the whole group by the unique subgroup of order $p$ in that factor is non-IYB.
item.dc:creator: L\"u Gong

item.title: An additively idempotent semiring of least order generating a limit variety
item.description: arXiv:2611.13944v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct an additively idempotent semiring of order five that generates a limit variety and is not strongly nonfinitely based. The generated variety has exactly two maximal proper subvarieties, both hereditarily finitely based. We also prove that no ai-semiring of order at most four generates a limit variety. Consequently, five is the least possible order of a finite ai-semiring generating a limit variety.
item.dc:creator: Qirui Ma, Mengya Yue

item.title: Automorphisms of the Reduced Finitary Power Monoid of $\N^d$
item.description: arXiv:2611.13956v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given an additive semigroup $S$, the collection of its nonempty finite subsets can be equipped with the setwise addition \[ X + Y = \{x + y : x \in X, \; y \in Y\}, \] forming a semigroup denoted by $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin}}(S)$, which is called the finitary power semigroup of $S$. If $S$ is a monoid with identity $0$, the finite nonempty subsets containing $0$ form a submonoid $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin},0}(S)$, known as the reduced finitary power monoid, whose identity element is the singleton $\{0\}$. Let $d$ be a positive integer, $\mathbb{N}$ the set of nonnegative integers, and $\mathbb{N}^d = \{(a_1, a_2, \dots, a_d) \mid a_i \in \mathbb{N}\}$. For the one-dimensional case \(d=1\), Tringali and Yan (\textit{J. Comb. Theory, Ser. A}, \textbf{209} (2025)) established that the only nontrivial automorphism of $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin},0}(\mathbb{N})$ is the involution $X \mapsto \max X - X$. In this paper, we focus on the higher-dimensional case $d \ge 2$. We prove that $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin},0}(\mathbb{N}^d)) \cong S_d$, meaning that every automorphism is inner, induced by a permutation of the coordinate directions. This reveals a sharp contrast with the one-dimensional setting, where non-inner symmetries exist.
item.dc:creator: Songnian Xu, Dein Wong

item.title: Invariant measures, Gelfand pairs and integral representations
item.description: arXiv:2611.14085v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that whenever a Gelfand pair acts cocompactly on a locally compact space, there is a measure relatively invariant under a "parabolic" subgroup. That result seems new even for simple Lie groups, in which case it admits a much more direct proof. Along the way, we obtain for general Gelfand pairs a variant of Furstenberg's invariant ray theorem for minimal parabolics. We use this to establish an integral representation theorem for positive spherical functions in complete generality, extending the Harish-Chandra representation. A similar representation theorem is given for positive harmonic functions.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Monod

item.title: Non-closed products in branch and weakly branch groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.14127v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the first Grigorchuk group and the Gupta-Sidki $3$-group are not double coset separable, disproving a conjecture of Grigorchuk, Leemann and Nagnibeda. More generally, every finitely generated regular branch group with bounded activity contains two finitely generated, profinitely closed subgroups with trivial intersection whose product is not closed. Every infinite finitely generated subgroup of the first Grigorchuk group or the Gupta-Sidki $3$-group also fails to be double coset separable. We extend the construction to the $p$-Basilica groups and, using polynomial activity, to the long-range group, whose derived subgroup we prove to be finitely generated. Under an additional hypothesis on finite quotients, we determine the closure of the product. Membership in the constructed product is decidable in the first Grigorchuk group.
item.dc:creator: Daniele D'Angeli, Emanuele Rodaro

item.title: Poisson boundaries of lattices in locally compact groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.14321v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a random walk on a general locally compact group we provide a discretization procedure transforming the walk to one on a lattice of the group, preserving the Poisson boundary and some finiteness of moments.
item.dc:creator: Antoine Derimay

item.title: Progression-free sets in class $2$ and arbitrary finite groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.14464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study progression-free sets in arbitrary finite groups. We transfer sharp upper bounds from abelian groups to nilpotent groups of class $2$, and from nilpotent groups to arbitrary groups. Combining a recent result of Raghavan with the author's theorem on large subgroups of class $2$ gives \[ r_3(G) \, \leq \, C \, |G|\exp\left( -c\frac{(\log|G|)^{1/6}}{(\log\log|G|)^{1/3}}\right) \] for every finite group as $|G|\to\infty$. This improves the estimates obtained by using the abelian subgroup supplied by Pyber's theorem.
item.dc:creator: Luca Sabatini

item.title: Property Gamma and McDuff Factors from Shift-Similar and Houghton-like Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.09227v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We initiate the study of von Neumann algebras of shift-similar and Houghton-like groups, introduced by Mallery and Zaremsky as analogs of self-similar and R\"over-Nekrashevych groups, respectively. Given a shift-similar group $G$ of permutations of $\mathbb{N}$, one can form the Houghton-like group $H_n(G)$, a ``mashup" of the classical Houghton group $H_n$ with $G$, which acts on $X_n$, the disjoint union of $n$ copies of $\mathbb{N}$. One main result is that when $G$ and the canonical shift map $\sigma$ admit a joint F\o lner sequence for their action on $\mathbb{N}$, then both group von Neumann algebras $L(G)$ and $L(H_n(G))$ are II$_1$ factors with property Gamma and hence $G$ and $H_n(G)$ are inner amenable. More generally, let $\Gamma$ be an ICC group of permutations preserving the ends of $X_n$. We prove that if the natural near action on $\mathbb{N}$ of the germs of almost permutations arising from $\Gamma$ along some ray is amenable, then $L(\Gamma)$ has property Gamma; if this group of germs is itself amenable, then $L(\Gamma)$ is McDuff. Then we construct a shift-similar group $G$, using property (T) groups with certain actions, such that neither $G$ nor $H_n(G)$ is inner amenable. Finally, we produce extremely broad and diverse sources of shift-similar groups satisfying the joint amenability condition. These examples come from residually finite groups and from wobbling groups of a variety of metric spaces. In particular, we completely characterize all metrics $d$ on $\mathbb{N}$ for which the wobbling group $W(\mathbb{N},d)$ is shift-similar in terms of a coarse geometric property---namely, that $\sigma^{-1}$ is bornologous with respect to $d$. As a consequence, this gives us necessary and sufficient conditions for when the wobbling group of any countable metric space admits a shift-similar embedding.
item.dc:creator: Eli Bashwinger, Patrick DeBonis

item.title: Thompson indices of knots and the invertibility problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.13208v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Jones showed that Thompson's group $F$ produces all unoriented links, and introduced its oriented subgroup $\vec{F}$, which produces all oriented links; the same holds for the Brown-Thompson group $F_3$ and its oriented subgroup $\vec{F}_3$. The corresponding Thompson indices measure the complexity of a knot in these groups, much as the braid index does for braid groups. In this article we prove that the span of the Jones polynomial plus $1$ is a lower bound for the $F$- and $\vec{F}$-index, and we give lower bounds for the $\vec{F}$- and $\vec{F}_3$-index in terms of the degrees of the HOMFLY-PT polynomial. We then compute the four indices (the $F$-, $F_3$-, $\vec{F}$- and $\vec{F}_3$-index) for the prime knots with at most 13 crossings, by an exhaustive enumeration of tree diagrams (up to 13 leaves for $F$, 17 for $\vec{F}$, with the HOMFLY-PT polynomials of all the diagrams with 19 leaves, and 9 and 11 for $F_3$ and $\vec{F}_3$) completed by targeted searches; every value is rigorously certified, by exact computations and by verified computations of hyperbolic structures in interval arithmetic. The $F$-index is determined for all knots with at most 11 crossings, the $\vec{F}$-index for all knots with at most 8 crossings, and the $F_3$- and $\vec{F}_3$-index for all knots with at most 12 crossings. The main outcome of these computations is that the oriented indices are sensitive to the orientation: we find hundreds of non-invertible knots $K$ whose reverse $K^r$ has a different $\vec{F}$- or $\vec{F}_3$-index, the smallest being $8_{17}$ (with $\vec{F}_3$-index $7$ and $9$). The $\vec{F}$-index also distinguishes the Conway knot from its mutant, the Kinoshita-Terasaka knot.
item.dc:creator: Valeriano Aiello

item.title: Surface subgroups with prescribed finite quotients
item.description: arXiv:2611.13458v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every finite quotient of a finite covolume Kleinian group $G$ can be realized by a surface subgroup. More precisely, given an epimorphism from $G$ onto a finite group $F$, there exists a surface subgroup that maps surjectively onto $F$. As a consequence, the union of the surface subgroups is dense in $G$ with respect to the profinite topology. We also apply this result to obtain more examples of atoroidal surface bundles with signature zero in the construction of Kent--Leininger.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Lafont, Zhenghao Rao, Hongbin Sun

item.title: Bounding the security of the Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash function
item.description: arXiv:2611.13459v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash functions are a family of Cayley hash functions indexed by an integer parameter $k\ge 2$. Hashes are matrices in $SL_2(p)$ where $p$ is a large prime. We present an attack which finds collisions of length $O(\log p)$ whose average-case time complexity is $O(p^{0.28})$ when $k=2$ and $O(p^{0.36})$ when $k=3$ under an assumption in the spirit of Zaremba's Conjecture on continued fractions. This is an improvement on the more general attacks of Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter which have average-case time complexity $O(\sqrt{p})$. For any $k$, the average-case time complexity of our attack is $O(p^{1-\delta_k+o(1)})$ where $\delta_k$ is the Hausdorff dimension of a certain Cantor set. This tends to $O(\sqrt{p})$ as $k\to\infty$, so our attack has time complexity comparable to Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter's attacks as $k$ grows. We give examples of collisions for large primes found by our attack when $k=2, 3$.
item.dc:creator: Eilidh McKemmie

item.title: On L\'{e}vy type subgroups of the symmetric group of $\omega$ associated with simple density functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.13653v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The L\'{e}vy group, introduced by L\'{e}vy in (L\'{e}vy (1951)), is defined by \[\mathcal{L} = \left\{\sigma\in aut : \lim_n \frac{|\{k\in n : \sigma(k)\notin n\}|}{n} = 0\right\},\] where $aut$ denotes the group of all permutations of $\omega$. This group happens to be closely connected with the notion of asymptotic density as it consists of permutations that map sets with an asymptotic density back to sets with the same density. Our aim is to replicate the construction by replacing $n$ in the denominator by $g(n)$ for a function $g:\omega\to [0,\infty)$ with $g(n)\to \infty$ (weight), which leads us a class of L\'{e}vy type groups. Specifically we define simple L\'{e}vy group with weight $g$ as \[\mathcal{L}_g = \left\{\sigma\in aut : \lim_n \frac{|\{k\in n : \sigma(k)\notin n\}|}{g(n)} = 0\right\}.\] As a natural consequence we first study its relationship with the notion of simple density functions (which had been introduced in \cite{gd2} as a general class of density functions by similar manner) paving way for the class of simple density functions and ideals $\mathcal{I}_g$. We have $\mathcal{L}_g = aut$ if and only if $n/g(n)\to 0$ (just like $\mathcal{I}_g = 2^{\omega}$ if and only if $n/g(n)\to 0$). The relation between simple density functions and simple L\'{e}vy groups is in expected line. What seems more interesting is the comparative study of these groups. We start with the relation between $\mathcal{L}$ and $\mathcal{L}_g$ and constructing suitable examples it is shown that strict inclusions and incomparability may occur. Finally we come up with an interesting observation that there are continuum many pairwise incomparable simple L\'{e}vy groups, each of which is incomparable with $\mathcal{L}$.
item.dc:creator: Pratulananda Das, Nur Alam

item.title: Coxeter cubes on the graph associahedron and separable elements
item.description: arXiv:2611.14178v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A Coxeter cube is a Boolean lattice inside a finite Coxeter group $W$ such that every square is a Coxeter square in the sense of Dyer and Wang. A Coxeter cube of full dimension based at the identity, which we call a based cube, is the same as a partition of the positive roots into inversion sets with one simple root in each block. These partitions were studied by Dimitrov, Gigliotti, Ossip, Paquette and Wehlau under the name of fine decompositions, and by Hohlweg and Pons as partitions of $w_0$. We show that the based cubes of $W$ form a point configuration in the graph associahedron $K(\Gamma)$ of the Coxeter diagram $\Gamma$ of $W$. The vertices of $K(\Gamma)$ are the based cubes whose blocks are parabolic. Every other based cube lies in the interior of an edge or of a cubical face, and we count the based cubes on each edge using the Coxeter arrangement. We also characterize the elements of $W$ that occur as vertices of based cubes. For the cubes at the vertices of $K(\Gamma)$ these are exactly the separable elements of Gaetz and Gao, and for arbitrary based cubes they satisfy a similar condition.
item.dc:creator: Harrison Gimenez, SuHo Oh

item.title: A Symmetrization for Almost Symmetric Numerical Semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.14268v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We characterize almost symmetric numerical semigroups in terms of their associated Young diagrams, showing that almost symmetry is equivalent to a simple numerical identity relating the genus, the type, and the number of small elements, and also to a combinatorial condition on the hook lengths of the diagram. We then introduce a symmetrization procedure that associates with each almost symmetric numerical semigroup a symmetric numerical set. This yields a map from the set of almost symmetric numerical semigroups to the set of symmetric numerical sets. We also present experimental data on the image of this map and on the proportion of its elements that are numerical semigroups. The results show, in particular, that the map is far from injective and that its image contains many numerical sets that are not semigroups.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Delgado, Meral S\"uer, Mehmet Ye\c{s}il

item.title: Uncountably many $2$-spherical groups of Kac-Moody type of rank $3$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$
item.description: arXiv:2504.17513v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we show that Weyl-invariant commutator blueprints of type $(4, 4, 4)$ are faithful. As a consequence we answer a question of Tits from the late $1980$s about twin buildings. Moreover, we obtain the first example of a $2$-spherical Kac-Moody group over a finite field which is not finitely presented.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Bischof

item.title: R-harmonious groups
item.description: arXiv:2512.08830v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A finite group $G$ of order $n$ is \emph{R-harmonious} if the non-identity elements of $G$ can be listed as $g_1,g_2,\dots,g_{n-1}$ so that the consecutive products $g_1g_2,g_2g_3,\dots,g_{n-1}g_1$ again list every non-identity element exactly once. Beals, Gallian, Headley and Jungreis proved that an abelian group is R-harmonious if and only if it does not have a unique element of order~$2$ and is not $\mathbb{Z}_3$. We prove a lifting lemma which shows that, under suitable conditions on $G/H$, a group $G$ with a normal subgroup $H$ of odd order is R-harmonious. As applications we show that every group of odd order whose abelianization is not an elementary abelian $3$-group is R-harmonious; in particular, every nontrivial group of odd order not divisible by~$3$ is R-harmonious. We also show that every split extension of a group of odd order by a ``harmoniously matched'' group is harmoniously matched, and hence R-harmonious. Together with a computer search, this gives many non-abelian even-order R-harmonious groups, among them the dihedral groups $D_{2n}$ with $n\equiv 8\pmod{16}$ or $n\equiv 16\pmod{32}$. Finally, we observe that the quaternion group $Q_8$ satisfies the Hall--Paige condition but is not R-harmonious.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: Subperiodic groups and bounded automorphisms of periodic graphs
item.description: arXiv:2605.12630v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A subperiodic group is a group of motions of $d$-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb R^d$ which contains a translation lattice $\mathbb Z^r$ of rank $r < d$ as a subgroup of finite index. Cayley graphs of subperiodic groups are used to illustrate the concept of bounded automorphisms (particularly of finite order), i.e. those when the distance between a graph vertex and its image has an upper bound. The description of subperiodic groups in dimension 3 in terms of subgroup structure and abstract group isomorphism types [75 crystallographic rod groups ($r=1$) and 80 layer groups ($r=2$) belong to 32 and 34 types, respectively] allows for a convenient characterization of bounded automorphisms of their Cayley graphs. An easy-to-compute set of invariants is developed for recognizing the isomorphism types of crystallographic groups in $\mathbb R^3$ from finite presentations which makes use of only the number of nonconjugate subgroups up to a given finite index $n$ ($n \leq 12$ for rod groups, $n \leq 8$ for layer groups, and $n \leq 24$ for space groups), and how many of them are normal. A criterion is proven that if a finite (inverse-closed) generating set of a group $G$ is stabilized by conjugation by a nontrivial element of finite order in $G$, then the respective Cayley graph possesses nontrivial bounded automorphisms of finite order. This criterion is applied to three-periodic sphere-packing graphs. Subperiodic groups in $\mathbb R^4$ with a three-dimensional translation lattice are used to systematically derive embeddings of three-periodic ladder graphs in $\mathbb R^3$.
item.dc:creator: Igor A. Baburin

item.title: Vietoris-Rips complexes of affine Coxeter groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.38703v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that all affine Coxeter groups admit contractible Vietoris-Rips complexes. More precisely, for any affine Coxeter group $W_a$ with standard generating set $S$, we prove that the Vietoris-Rips complex $\mathcal{VR}_t(W_a;S)$ is contractible for all sufficiently large $t$. We also investigate other finitely generated groups of the form $G=H\rtimes F$ for $F$ finite, and prove that for any finite symmetric generating set $A$ for $H$ such that $A^F=A$, the complexes $\mathcal{VR}_t(G;AF)$ and $\mathcal{VR}_t(H;A)$ are homotopy equivalent for all $t\ge 1$.
item.dc:creator: Riley Decker, Matthew C. B. Zaremsky

item.title: Slim Polygons, Hyperbolicity, and a new Quasi-Isometric Invariant
item.description: arXiv:2611.09078v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the slimness function, $\mathrm{Slim}_X(n)$, of a geodesic metric space, which records the maximal slimness of its geodesic polygons as a function of the number of sides. We study the large-scale behaviour of this function and its relation to hyperbolicity, growth function, and quasi-isometries. We first establish that the slimness function is a natural quasi-isometric invariant in the hyperbolic setting. We then obtain quantitative estimates for geodesic polygons in hyperbolic spaces and bounded-valency graphs. In particular, we show that sufficiently slow growth of the slimness function forces tree-like geometry. We also prove a decomposition result for trees of hyperbolic spaces. We show that for a finitely generated hyperbolic group $G$ there are only two possibilities: either $G$ is virtually free and $\operatorname{Slim}_G$ is bounded, or $\operatorname{Slim}_G(n)\simeq\log n$. Finally, we investigate the interaction between polygonal slimness and the growth of connected bounded-valency graphs. Combining the resulting estimates with large-scale dimension theory, we obtain criteria implying that an unbounded graph has asymptotic dimension one.
item.dc:creator: Panagiotis Tselekidis

item.title: On identities in connected topological groups
item.description: arXiv:2406.05203v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a connected (indeed, path-connected) Hausdorff topological group G such that, for an odd n >= 665, the identity x^n = e holds in some neighbourhood of the identity but does not hold in the whole group. This answers in the negative a question of Mycielski and Aronszajn (Question 2.48 of the Kourovka Notebook). The construction uses the Graev extension of metrics to free topological groups and results of Adian and Adian-Atabekyan (for n > 10^10, alternatively, of Ol'shanskii and Ashmanov-Ol'shanskii) on free Burnside groups and their central extensions.
item.dc:creator: I. N. Zyabrev, E. A. Reznichenko

item.title: Partial sequencings and other combinatorial aspects of large groups
item.description: arXiv:2511.19285v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A \emph{partial sequencing} of length $k$ in a finite group $G$ is a sequence $g_0,g_1,\dots,g_{k-1}$ of distinct elements of $G$ with $g_0=1_G$ such that the partial products $g_0,\, g_0g_1,\,\dots,\, g_0g_1\cdots g_{k-1}$ are also distinct. Partial R-sequencings and partial harmonious sequences are defined similarly. Using the recent work of M\"uyesser and Pokrovskiy, we determine when such partial sequences extend to full ones in sufficiently large groups. In particular, if $G$ is sufficiently large and $k\le\sqrt{|G|}$, then a partial sequencing of length $k$ extends to a sequencing of $G$ if and only if some element of $G$ that is not one of its partial products has the same image in the abelianization as the product of all elements of $G$. This holds automatically when the commutator subgroup has more than $k$ elements, and we show that it can fail otherwise. Using the fact that every group of odd order has a symmetric harmonious sequence, we also prove that $\mathbb{Z}_{2^k}\times H$ is doubly R-sequenceable for every group $H$ of odd order, unless it is $\mathbb{Z}_2$ (in particular, every abelian group other than $\mathbb{Z}_2$ is), that $K\times H$ is symmetric sequenceable whenever $K$ is, that all sufficiently large groups are doubly sequenceable, doubly R-sequenceable, doubly harmonious and doubly $\#$-harmonious, and we verify these four properties for all groups of order $4$ to $12$ and for several small dihedral and dicyclic groups.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: On Boston's Unramified Conjecture for $\mathrm{GL}_2$ and McLeman's $(3,3)$-Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2609.37252v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $A$ be a complete Noetherian commutative local ring with finite residue field of characteristic $p$. Let $G_{\mathbf{Q}}$ be the absolute Galois group of the rational number field and fix an inertia subgroup $I_p\subset G_{\mathbf{Q}}$ at $p$. We prove that every continuous odd representation $\rho:G_{\mathbf{Q}}\to\mathrm{GL}_2(A)$, unramified outside finitely many primes and with finite $\rho(I_p)$, has finite image if $p>3$ or $A$ has positive characteristic. For $p=3$, the conclusion also holds when the local representation at $3$ is reducible, or the local residual semisimplification has no mod-$3$ cyclotomic self-twist. In particular, this proves the two-dimensional odd case of Boston's unramified Fontaine--Mazur conjecture over $\mathbf{Q}$ for every odd $p$. Furthermore, we deduce finiteness results for conjugate self-dual representations of pro-$p$ Galois groups over imaginary quadratic fields under a ramification condition, and for representations of their unramified pro-$p$ groups of generator rank at most two. As an application, we resolve the sufficiency direction of McLeman's $(3,3)$-conjecture on $p$-class field towers for $p>3$. Namely, we prove that if $K$ is an imaginary quadratic field with $p$-class rank two and the Galois group $\mathrm{Gal}(K_{\varnothing}(p)/K)$ of the maximal unramified $p$-extension of $K$ has Zassenhaus type $(3,3)$, then the $p$-class field tower of $K$ is finite. For $p=3$, we also rule out infinite towers for ten of the thirteen fourth Zassenhaus quotients classified by Ahlqvist and Pink.
item.dc:creator: Yufan Luo
